headline.title: Pre-season: still too mild.
headline.text: None of the resorts close to opening get cold enough to make snow this week. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Warm temperatures continue through Wednesday with potential for highs exceeding a few daily records Wednesday afternoon.
Light rain showers are possible on Tuesday afternoon and evening, then widespread rain is expected Thursday into Friday morning.
Precip lingers for several days behind the cold front

ALY.excerpt:
) Above normal temperatures and mainly dry weather expected today through Wednesday.
) A cold front will bring increasing chances for some beneficial showers Thursday, followed by additional chances for rain Friday into the weekend.

GYX.excerpt:
Outside of some shower activity in the mountains and foothills, conditions will stay mostly dry through mid week with above normal temperatures.
The first chance in several weeks of a soaking rainfall arrives late this week.

BUF.excerpt:
) Unusually warm weather is expected this Tuesday and Wednesday, with forecast temperatures potentially reaching record highs for early November.
) There is high probability of widespread showers as a cold front arrives Wednesday night through Thursday. Unsettled weather is expected to continue into the weekend.

PHI.excerpt:
Aside from potential for nocturnal fog development tonight and Tuesday night, generally tranquil weather is expected to prevail through the middle of the week.
The next chance for rain returns late this week and into the weekend.

CTP.excerpt:
) Unseasonably mild and dry weather will continue until late Wednesday Night.
) Periods of showers preceding and accompanying a cold frontal passage. Cooler and a return to mainly dry conditions will follow for Friday through Sunday.

RLX.excerpt:
) Light rain showers gradually peter out this evening, followed by brief dry weather on Tuesday.
) Turning active once again on Wednesday with a cold frontal passage. Unsettled weather and much colder temperatures advertised for this weekend.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Quiet and mild.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:31}} to {{t:58}}, with rain at times.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Nights stay too mild to make much snow this week.
NWS Burlington forecasters, Monday 1:31 PM: "Warm temperatures continue through Wednesday with potential for highs exceeding a few daily records Wednesday afternoon."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.
